thread:
anya: FYI I'm seeing a bunch of failed GPU node creations in us-west-2 this morning. deploy bot is spitting rate errors when trying to attach SGs.
sam: Can you paste the deploy log? seeing the same in canary stack
anya: deploy-bot: ERROR provisioning instance i-xxx: "RequestLimitExceeded: Request limit exceeded for security-group-modification" when calling ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute
mike: Oof, that's the API throttle on EC2 SecurityGroup operations. We recently spun up parallel bootstrapping for Dedicated pools, so we're hitting AWS per-account request rate.
lee: Which region / instance type? Any specific SG rules that explode counts? (we have a limit of 1000 rules per account in some regions)
anya: us-west-2, mostly g5.2xlarge and p4d. We're creating ~80 security-group changes concurrently per AZ. Most SGs are per-deployment (we tried to isolate customer traffic).
sam: That explains it. AWS enforces both total SGs and modify request rate. The two relevant errors: "SecurityGroupLimitExceeded" and intermittent "RequestLimitExceeded" for ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute.
mike: Short-term workaround: pause concurrent node bootstraps and reuse a shared set of SGs for canary nodes. Longer-term: request AWS quota increase + ask for burst allowance on API rate.
anya: I tried opening a case but Support asked for traffic patterns and exact error timestamps. I have a list of timestamps, how we parallelized, and the deploy job ids.
cloudops-bot: support-case: 1234567890 created with AWS. Initial response: need CAPABILITY to raise EC2 API request rates; expected 72h review.
lee: 72h is risky. Can we throttle our own deployment loops? e.g. add jitter + concurrency cap to the fleet-provisioner.
sam: Yes, pushing a quick change to the provisioner to reduce parallelism from 20->4 per AZ and exponential backoff on SG attach. I'll open a PR and feature flag it.
anya: Please do. Also we should pre-create a pool of 100 shared SGs per AZ and tag them for reuse; that reduces number of ModifyNetworkInterfaceAttribute calls.
mike: Agreed. Pre-creating reduces API churn but costs more in SG count. Need to check SG rule limits: per SG 60 rules default, and per account rule quota varies.
lee: AWS recommended combining IPs into fewer rules and using prefix lists where possible. For customer isolation we can use AWS NACLs or route-based isolation in some cases.
anya: Another issue: our infra creates a new SG per ephemeral job because of our repo-per-tenant design. Let's change allocation to tenant-shared SGs for short-lived jobs.
sam: PR: https://git.redwood.dev/provisioner/compare/ reduce-concurrency-jitter. Rolling out to canary now.
cloudops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout paused automatically after 7 failures (SG attach errors).
mike: For the support case, AWS asked for: sample API request ids, timestamps, region, approximate QPS. I compiled a CSV and attached to case 1234567890.
aws-support: Hi team — AWS here. We've escalated the case. We can increase the ModifyNetworkInterface API request rate and advise SG bucket planning. Please provide expected concurrency and a peak 15-minute window.
anya: Sent peak numbers: ~120 ModifyNetworkInterface requests/sec at peak across region during scale-up. Also attached our deployment job IDs.
aws-support: Thanks — we provisionally increased request rate limit for your account in us-west-2. Please monitor for 24h and confirm. Case 1234567890.
mike: Great. Still want the infra change though; don't want to rely on provider exceptions.
lee: Also let's add alerting: when we see >50/second SG-modify API errors fire a P0 slack alert to eng-infra and harm minimization runbook.
sam: Adding a circuit breaker in provisioner to backoff + reuse SGs. Will push hotfix in 30m.
anya: After enabling reuse + lower concurrency, failures stopped in canary. I'll kick a small Dedicated pool to validate further.
mike: Cost note: sharing SGs means more careful rule management; could increase rule count per SG and might force us to ask for higher per-account rule quotas too. Add that to the support thread.
anya: Noted. I'll append a request to aws case for SG count and rules-per-SG increases as a follow-up.
sam: TL;DR: immediate mitigation: reduce parallel SG ops, pre-create shared SG pool, exponential backoff. Long-term: quota increases and refactor tenant isolation model.
lee: Thanks team. I'll update runbooks and schedule a retrospective to re-evaluate per-tenant infra patterns.
anya: Thanks all :thumbsup:
